purpose: Immutable prior comparison baseline for reproducible stream/fs source-coverage accounting; not shared annotation data.

rows: Both split device/path and use a two-word interface/backend handle. CVX also has 40 wrappers and 32 registered devices; Outbreak adds path-resolution/rewrite behavior. This supports the API role, not all failure-path equivalence.
Both release the wrapper only after a callable Close returns; missing Close diagnoses and retains it.
Both dispatch through method +0x1C on the backend handle, with zero fallback.
Both use method +0x18 for handle/offset/origin. This is the virtual filesystem layer, not a host seek syscall.
Method +0x20 forwards a read request; neither API name establishes synchronous completion.
Method +0x24 forwards a write request with zero fallback.
Method +0x28 stops transfer without releasing the wrapper.
Method +0x2C and invalid-handle fallback 3 agree with CVE_FS_ST_ERR=3 in the CVX header.
Method +0x30 is the sector-length query, distinct from byte size and transfer progress.
Same +0x38 dispatch. Both owned Outbreak providers return bytes from completed sectors only in state1; CVX concrete providers instead expose their seek/Tell cursor times2048 without a state guard.
Full split/default/three original arguments/+0x48/duplicated IsExistFile diagnostic supports qualified alias; Outbreak additionally rewrites scratch path, but still forwards original arguments.

Both use method +0x60, but CVX source invokes it with only the backend object while Outbreak preserves optional arguments. CVX's old-style function-pointer declarations cannot establish Outbreak's complete callback ABI.
Both use method +0x64; same optional-argument/old-style prototype limitation as OptFn1. Do not copy the apparent one-argument call.

Outbreak leaves a1 and other argument registers unchanged when replacing a0 with the backend object. CVX source passes only the object despite its public two-argument prototype. Do not drop the Outbreak length argument.

Private CVX helper matches full strlen/input-length-prefix/32-device scan/first-callable/default0 legacy route and no explicit callback arguments. Outbreak adds capability selector64 and optional selector4; no NULL aggregation, provider implementation or extension-result unit is proved.
Same resolved-path +8 size query, but Outbreak adds rewrite/default fallback; its NULL-interface diagnostic can return into a NULL +8 load, unlike CVX explicit return.
Same resolved-path +0x5C plus original second argument. Outbreak adds resolver behavior and may continue to NULL +0x5C load after its returning diagnostic.
Complete 32-slot registry scan and nonnull interface/method0 guards agree; candidate alias now recorded on the existing authoritative row.
CVX's default handler spins forever; Outbreak forwards SJUNI Error to its diagnostic path. An identical error-handler name does not establish noreturn behavior.

Both have 64 objects, caller-supplied 16-byte nodes, four queue heads and split/merge mode. CVX casts work size to unsigned before division; the Outbreak notebook records signed truncation. Invalid inputs need separate treatment.
Clear the object, retaining caller ownership of nodes/payload storage; no freeing of borrowed buffers.
Both relink the external node free list and clear four heads. Both initialize a final node even when no valid positive node count has been established.
Sum payload lengths for a selected queue; this returns bytes, not node count.
Whole-front-span removal returns its node to the free list; a smaller request only splits in mode 1. Payload bytes are borrowed, not copied.
Append or merge a physically adjacent tail in mode 1; exhausted node pool reports an error. This is queue publication, not a payload copy.
Prepend or merge adjacent head in mode 1, using an external free node when needed. No proof the span is the last reservation.
Returns the entire first-span length through output; mode 1 allows length>=request, other modes require equality. Different from the ring's min(request,available) output.
Count selected queue nodes, without the bounds checking of GetNumData.
Count nodes remaining in the free list; not free payload bytes.
Both first-reference initializers clear64 records of48 bytes (0x30) and increment a module count. No payload allocation or new per-object initialization is established.
Both decrement without an initial zero guard and clear the fixed object pool only on exact new zero; neither frees caller-owned node or payload arrays.

Both return the constructor-installed UUID pointer. The sixteen owned bytes23DA78 equal the pinned source UUID serialized as PS2 little-endian <IHH8B; this does not establish universal object/ABI equivalence.
Both install callback/context at object offsets28/2C without invoking them. Shared fields and exact UUID support the interface role; callback lifetime/reentry remain caller contracts.

Both split a pointer/length descriptor with signed min, make an empty remainder pointer null, and support the observed input/prefix alias ordering. No byte copy or negative-size validation is established.
CVX spins forever; Outbreak reports its owned SJRB Error through a diagnostic helper.
Same borrowed-buffer/capacity/wrap-extension concept, but CVX has 64 objects of 0x30 bytes; Outbreak has 256 objects of 0x40 bytes, four added transfer counters and shifted callback fields.
Both reset positions, readable=0 and free=capacity. Outbreak additionally clears four transfer totals.
Selector 0 reports free bytes, selector 1 readable bytes; invalid selector reports error and returns zero.
Same bounded grant and modulo position advance. Outbreak also updates acquisition totals and uses its own tagged guard.
Both publish/return capacity and maintain wrap-extension mirror copies; Outbreak adds per-pool return totals.
Both verify the modulo previous position before restoring capacity. Outbreak also subtracts acquisition totals after a returning diagnostic, including a mismatch path.
Peek contiguous grant, report whether request fits and avoid moving positions. Preserve invalid-selector and zero-request edge behavior.
Returns configured capacity, not readable/free count or extension allocation size.
Returns caller-provided wrap-extension length. This API requires separately allocated backing extent.
Both clear on first module reference, then increment. Outbreak adds the shared tag1 guard and has256 records of64 bytes (0x40); CVX has64 records of48 bytes (0x30).
Both decrement and clear on exact zero; Outbreak has an added tag1 guard and a larger pool. Neither walks live buffers or frees borrowed payload storage.

Both guard, zero a nonnull object and mark it unused, retaining caller ownership of the buffer. Outbreak clears64 bytes (0x40), while the CVX32-bit source layout is48 bytes (0x30); no cross-version struct cast is justified.
Both return the installed UUID. All16 owned bytes23DA58 exactly match the pinned source UUID; Outbreak still differs in record size, pool size, counters and error callback offsets.
Both set callback/context, but Outbreak fields are38/3C and CVX fields28/2C. The latter positions hold Outbreak transfer counters.
Both return the borrowed backing-buffer pointer at1C. No allocation, length validation or ownership transfer occurs.
Unsigned id<8 selects a fixed context slot; returning it does not establish active state.
RPC function 2 sends four 32-bit words and receives one remote handle. Transport status is not independently validated.
RPC function 3 sends the remote handle with no returned payload; local state clearing is separate.

Both enforce EE64/IOP32 alignment, 64-byte length multiples, eight slots and a 64-byte footer. Outbreak explicitly sets an enabled flag consumed by its service gate; CVX Create does not set that flag.
Store completion callback/context at +0x20/+0x24; completion occurs when a newer footer sequence is observed.
Store fill callback/context at +0x28/+0x2C, invoked before cache synchronization and DMA submission.
Both acknowledge a newer signed footer sequence before refill and submission. Outbreak additionally requires enabled and global initialization gates; its teardown depends on these gates.
CVX immediately requests remote destruction and clears the object. Outbreak first disables submission and pumps ALL contexts until its in-flight flag clears, without a timeout.
Scan eight active records under the shared stream critical section. Each record can invoke callbacks and submit DMA, so loop count is not a duration bound.
Both clear callback/context pairs20/24 and28/2C. This operation neither waits for inflight work nor destroys/deactivates the context; full destruction is a separate operation.

Both default receive callbacks increment an otherwise unqueried local static counter. Outbreak constructor/indirect dispatch binds this to newer-sequence acknowledgement completion, not every DMA submission or a user callback.

Both default fill callbacks write0xAA, format Hello from EE (%d) into the payload using a separate local counter and then increment it. Formatting is not size-bounded locally; actual application callbacks can differ.

Related filename-size purpose only: Outbreak uses two optional CA/CB halves with original name plus resolved-path argument, and lacks a NULL resolver guard; CVX calls ordinary +8 once and has no such 64-bit API here.

Related size-with-parameter purpose only: Outbreak performs uninitialized stack device lookup before splitting, then CC/CD half queries. CVX explicit initialization/validation cannot be substituted as proof of intended admission.
Both return byte quantities, but Outbreak uses completed-count+0x14 only in state1. CVX returns req_nsct*2048 without state guard; that same field is modified by Seek and returned by Tell.
Outbreak returns completed-count+0x28 shifted11 only in state1; CVX returns Seek/Tell req_nsct*2048 regardless of state. Neither getter alone proves completion of arbitrary pending I/O.
Owned interface +8 is a signed-low32 adapter around wider13B330. CVX exposes a Sint32 cached/open/seek-end/close query directly and has no CA..CD optional methods.
Shared partition/member resolution and sector-byte sizing. CVX opens a new stream; Outbreak reconfigures existing stream+4 with richer parent/path bounds and rejects status4.
Both log operation2, create a record, delegate partition/member setup, close on negative setup and return NULL on failure. Child stream contracts and guards differ.
CVX is a field getter. Outbreak conditionally refreshes oversized cached metadata, always queries stream bytes on remaining valid paths, divides signed toward zero by2048 and can return-5.
CVX returns fsize and preserves NULL -3. Outbreak shifts the result of129C08 by11, including errors (-3 becomes -6144), so this is sector-derived bytes rather than an exact unpadded byte field.

Shared validated path/parent/range output and cumulative16-bit member lengths; Outbreak additionally selects32-bit lengths by descriptor+F, adds descriptor+114 base, and does not walk CVX linked additive partitions.
